full_judgment: 5. Mr Uzzal Bhowmick, learned Advocate for the appellants takes us through the materials on record and submits that the plaintiff although claimed that Dinu Mondal was the original owner of the suit land but they failed to lead any positive evidence supporting the contention. Admittedly CS record was prepared in the name of Dukhi Bewa showing his share to the extent of 8 annas. The presumption of preparation of CS record is to be rebuted by the plaintiff through evidence. Subsequently, 2(two) records were prepared in conformity of the CS record. In SA record the names of the husbands of 2(two) daughters of Dukhi Bewa were recorded with the name of some other title less persons and RS record was prepared in the name of Ashwini Kumar Mondal to the extent of 8 annas share which supports that Dukhi Bewa obtained the suit land as Yatuka and it was her stridhana. Although, the said claim of the defendants about Stridhana was incorporated by amended of the written statement at a belated stage but it was nothing but a better statement. The defendants proved their case by Exhibiting CS, SA and RS khatian Exhibits-Ka-Gha. He refers to the deed of purchase of the plaintiffs predecessor Exhibit-5 and submits that through the said documents the plaintiff processor purchased land from 3 plots to the extent of 8 arenas share of each plot. The plaintiffs thus admitted the title of 8 annas share of the defendant Ashwani over the suit land. While the sons of Sahachari admitted the title of the defendant to the extent of 8 annas share, their sons cannot undo those after expiry of long years. He refers to the statement of paragraph-Cha of the written statement and submits that Dukhi Bewa in the year 1940 partitioned of the suit land between his 2(two) daughters which has been admitted by PW2 and supported by the evidence of DW 4. The plaintiff did not deny it by cross-examining DW 4. The title and possession over the suit land has been admitted by the first generation, second generation and third generation, now the plaintiffs being fourth generation cannot disown it. The subsequent 2 records, i.e., SA and RS support the aforesaid partition by Dukhi Bewa. It is admitted position of fact that Ashwani Kumar being the son of Gayashwari transferred more than 4 annas share of the suit land. The plaintiffs' present suit without challenging those documents and claiming title over the suit land and without making any prayer for correction of the record of rights is not maintainable. The facts and circumstances and the transfer by Ashwani Kumar proves that he got the suit land per stripes. The trial Court without entering into the facts and evidence on record erred in law and thereby decreed the suit which is to be interfered with by this Court in this appeal.
